subject: Dedicated GPU burst scheduling + on-call handshake for Skyline Health
messages:
From: Amira Blake <amira@skylinehealth.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Jorge Ramos <jorge.ramos@skylinehealth.ai>, procurement@skylinehealth.ai
Date: 2029-06-03T09:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU burst scheduling + on-call handshake for Skyline Health

Thanks for the call this morning, Vanessa. Quick recap and a couple asks from our infra team.

Recap: we like the Dedicated pool sizing you proposed (12 persistent GPUs / 4 preemptible shoulder) but need clarity on how burst will be scheduled across regions and what triggers prewarm vs. fallback to lower-capacity models.

Outstanding asks:
- Can you provide an ops-level schedule for burst admission (how many requests/sec to allow per minute per pool)?
- What does Redwood expect us to keep in our on-call rotation vs. what Redwood will handle for capacity incidents?
- We need the SLA template with the burst credit cliff and the proposed eviction window for long-running jobs.

Attaching our procurement checklist; Jorge will follow up with a specific list of telemetry fields they need.

—Amira
Director of Product, Skyline Health

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Amira Blake <amira@skylinehealth.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-06-03T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU burst scheduling + on-call handshake for Skyline Health

Amira — thanks, and great meeting. Quick answers up-front, then a proposal below.

High-level: Redwood will manage admission and routing for the Dedicated pool for production traffic. You get: pinned persistent capacity (12 GPUs), shoulder preemptible layer (4 GPUs), and a cross-region transient burst lane we can authorize on demand (up to +8 GPUs for 10-minute windows).

Proposal (ops-level):
- Burst admission policy: token bucket per-customer with a default refill of 120k tokens/hour and cost-weighted token consumption per request type (small gen = 10 tokens, long-ctx = 150 tokens). That maps to rough RPS limits but gives us throttling headroom.
- Prewarm trigger: when 80% token consumption predicted over the next 5m OR sustained queue depth > 6 requests for 90s. Prewarm will spin per-model warm workers (expected 45–90s warm).
- Fallback: if prewarm not available we route to a compatible quantized variant (same model family) with degraded latency but same semantic quality band.
- Eviction window: long-running jobs (>=180s) are candidates for graceful eviction after an additional 60s retry; eviction credits apply per month (see attached SLA appendix).

On-call handshake (what Redwood handles vs. customer):
- Redwood: admission, autoscale orchestration, fallback routing, and platform-side alerts (we will run the first-line capacity escalation). We provide runbook links and a 24/7 escalation path for capacity incidents tied to the SLA.
- Skyline: we ask you to own application-level mitigation (rate-limiting at edge) and postmortem coordination if Skyline product logic causes unusual traffic patterns.

Deliverables I can share by end of day: a one-page ops schedule mapping tokens -> RPS per pool, a draft SLA appendix with credit cliff language, and a short on-call playbook that defines the 3-step escalation. Marcus can include kernel-level limits for GPU packing.

If that works I’ll drop the 1-pager and SLA into the Drive link and we can iterate.

—Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Director, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Amira Blake <amira@skylinehealth.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Jorge Ramos <jorge.ramos@skylinehealth.ai>
Date: 2029-06-03T13:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU burst scheduling + on-call handshake for Skyline Health

Amira — adding a few technical specifics, per Vanessa’s note, so your infra team can validate:

- GPU packing: persistent 12 GPUs will be packed for steady-state low-latency work. Shoulder preemptible GPUs are isolated to a separate node pool with a strict preemption policy (preemptible eviction priority).
- Burst lane sizing: the +8 transient GPUs are region-agnostic but bound by a cross-region quota. We plan to use locality-aware routing to prefer the same AZ and then spill to secondary region if local capacity is exhausted.
- Warm vs. cold startup: warm workers use a lightweight checkpoint with KV-cache priming; warm time 45–90s depending on model seq length. Cold startup may take 4–6 minutes. We’ll tag requests with warmness hints so Skyline can prioritize mission-critical flows.
- Telemetry fields (minimal set we’ll push to your SIEM): model_id, model_variant, request_id, tokens_consumed, queue_time_ms, prewarm_trigger, eviction_attempts, region_served.

Attaching a short template for the admission token table and an example mapping to RPS for a 512-token average usage. Let us know if you want the numbers tuned to your actual prompt mix.

—Karthik
Head of Dedicated Platform, Redwood Inference

From: Jorge Ramos <jorge.ramos@skylinehealth.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Amira Blake <amira@skylinehealth.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-06-04T08:14:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU burst scheduling + on-call handshake for Skyline Health

Thanks — this is helpful. A couple follow-ups from our infra team:
1) Can you confirm the cross-region spill latency penalty we should budget for? (rough p50/p95 numbers when spilling to secondary region).
2) For eviction: will Redwood provide a graceful callback so our agent can checkpoint before preemption? We’d like to avoid lost state for healthcare workflows.

Also, procurement prefers a 30-day review period on the SLA appendix before commitments. Can we get a draft SLA by EOD today to start internal review?

—Jorge
Infra Lead, Skyline Health

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Jorge Ramos <jorge.ramos@skylinehealth.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Amira Blake <amira@skylinehealth.ai>
Date: 2029-06-04T16:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU burst scheduling + on-call handshake for Skyline Health

Jorge — quick answers and attachments.

- Cross-region spill latency: measured p50 ~ 45ms extra, p95 ~ 210ms extra for our EU-US pairs; for US-us-east <-> us-west we expect p50 ~ 28ms, p95 ~ 120ms. I included a microbench we ran with the model family you mentioned.
- Graceful callback: yes. We expose a preemption webhook with 60s TTL where customers can attempt a single checkpoint. The agent can also read a "preempt_count" header. We recommend doing lightweight KV flush on that callback rather than full model state dumps.
- Draft SLA: attached (SLA_Appendix_Skyline_v0.3.docx). Key callouts: 6 burst credits per month (10-minute windows), credit cliff at 85% monthly consumption, and compensating credits for sustained inability to allocate burst capacity.

Next steps: Vanessa — I think we should schedule a 30-minute ops walkthrough with Jorge and Amira next week to walk the runbook and show the preemption webhook behavior. I’ll also drop the admission token table into the Drive.

—Marcus Lin
Senior Engineering Manager, Dedicated Runtime, Redwood Inference
